mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or Superintendencia de Sociedades of the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by certified Spanish translation by a sworn translator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU terrorist financing and sanctions lists, and Colombian domestic watchlists (UIAF reports, Procuraduría and Fiscalía disclosures). Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds declaration, senior management approval, and ongoing monitoring. Payments rails (Stripe, Wise) must not be opened until PEP and sanctions clearance is archived in the corporate AML file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (rues.org.co) and the corresponding local Cámara de Comercio online platform, e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (ccb.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed company names must be in Spanish or use recognizably Latin-script characters; accents and the letter ñ are respected. Foreign-language names are permissible only if they are descriptive and include a Spanish-language complement, and they must not create homonymy or confusion with existing registered names. All registry filings, statutes, and public documents must be executed in Spanish; for international branding, a Latin-script transliteration may be registered descriptively but not as a unique corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Cámara de Comercio rejects a proposed company name on grounds of homonymy, misleading similarity, or use of a reserved token, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición' before the same Chamber within 10 business days of notification, attaching additional distinctive elements or explaining why the token is appropriate. If the Chamber upholds the rejection, the applicant may submit an 'apelación' to the Superintendencia de Sociedades, or seek judicial review before the administrative contentious jurisdiction. During pendency, reservation of an alternative name should be secured to avoid delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for an S.A.S. in AI post-production and subtitle services. The registered office must be a real physical address in Colombia capable of receiving judicial and business notifications; a purely postal 'letterbox' address without personnel or records is not acceptable. A virtual office or co-working address with dedicated rooms, meeting space, and mail handling is accepted if the lease or service contract and the local floor location are documented and disclosed to the Chamber of Commerce.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% to 10% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by DIAN (tax office) or the Cámara de Comercio for a low-risk, non-licensed service entity. The probability rises to 35% or more if invoices are issued materially inconsistent with the registered economic activity, if the company reports no employees but performs substantial operations, or if the registered address is a known virtual office without operative staffing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official portal: https://www.dian.gov.co; transactional services through MUISCA and the DIAN user authentication platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must incorporate or register the Colombian S.A.S. before the Chamber of Commerce, appoint a legal representative, then complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) process with DIAN to obtain the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT). The foreign shareholder must evidence capital contribution in foreign currency if applicable, obtain an electronic signature certificate issued by a DIAN-authorized certification authority, and register for mandatory electronic invoicing and all applicable taxes through DIAN's virtual user facility. A non-domiciled foreign entity with Colombian taxable activities must obtain an NIT through a designated agent or representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no check-the-box regime. The S.A.S. is automatically subject to entity-level income tax and VAT. Qualifying taxpayers may elect the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) for an integrated CIT/VAT determination subject to turnover limits. Foreign-controlled S.A.S. entities may elect Colombian Holding Company (CIN) status under Law 1943/2018 and Law 2069/2020 with respect to certain foreign-source dividends and capital gains. Hybrid mismatch rules under Article 120-3 of the Colombian Tax Statute disallow deductions for arrangements producing double non-taxation, but such elections are not relevant to ordinary subtitle production activities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to an S.A.S.; every S.A.S. engaged in any IVA-taxable activity must register from its first taxable operation. For natural persons, the simplified IVA regime has a threshold of gross income not exceeding 3,500 UVT in the immediately preceding taxable year, but this does not apply to corporate entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All S.A.S. VAT taxpayers must issue electronic sales invoices (factura electrónica de venta) through DIAN-authorized software providers or internal billing systems connected to DIAN through web services/API. Each invoice is transmitted to DIAN in XML format for real-time fiscal validation and receives a CUNE (Código Único de Numeración de Factura) or CUDE, alongside encryption of the invoice traceability code. A QR code and electronic stamp are integral to the valid invoice. No physical stamp is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for the 0% VAT rate when the exportation is genuine and covered by a Colombian customs export declaration. Export of services qualifies for 0% IVA when the recipient is legally domiciled or resident outside Colombia, the service is actually used or exploited exclusively abroad, remuneration is paid from abroad, and the service would otherwise be subject to Colombian IVA. AI subtitle transcription and voice cloning services supplied to foreign media or technology clients can qualify as exported services if the place of use and commercial benefit is outside Colombia. Services used locally in Colombia or rendered to Colombian-domiciled recipients are taxable at 19%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Valid Colombian customs export declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX) for goods; for services, a service export declaration or equivalent DIAN export registration where applicable
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods; for services, a signed contract and service-completion certificate proving use and benefit outside Colombia
Commercial invoice and export-priced electronic sales invoice with CUNE/QR code
Certificate of foreign exchange liquidation (Certificado de Liquidación de Divisas) or inward remittance certificate from the Colombian intermediary bank
RUT and NIT evidencing the exporter's tax registration
Payment receipt from the foreign client and proof of funds repatriation to Colombia
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN has full authority to examine export VAT refunds, including retrospective reviews generally covering the previous five tax years. If zero-rating is claimed without documentary substantiation, the taxpayer must repay the VAT refunded, plus indexation and default interest, and is subject to a penalty of up to 200% of the improperly claimed or refunded amount under Article 648 of the Colombian Tax Statute. Fraudulent overstatement of export zero-rating or false documentation to obtain VAT refunds can be prosecuted as tax crime under Law 1943/2018, exposing responsible parties to prison terms and disqualification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), acting as the central bank and foreign exchange authority under the Organic Statute of the Financial System and Resolution 017/2016; the Comité de Cambios and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) provide complementary regulatory and enforcement oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is convertible for its non-resident capital account though all foreign exchange transactions must be channeled through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries (IFCs) on the 'Mercado Cambiario'. Current-account transactions, including profit remittances and service payments, are widely permitted without individual prior approval, provided the underlying transaction is genuine, properly registered with Banco de la República where required (e.g., foreign investment declarations), and settled through an IFC. Capital-account transactions remain subject to registration and documentary compliance, and profit remittance is legal but will be subject to the 7% dividend withholding tax when paid to a non-resident beneficial owner absent a reduced treaty rate. The practical hurdles are documentation, timeliness, and ensuring the payment is declared under the correct form and settlement code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombian exchange rules require that export proceeds from both goods and services be brought into the country through the foreign exchange market within a maximum term of 180 days from the date of shipment or from the date the service is fully rendered, unless an extended term is granted by Banco de la República (generally up to six additional months upon justified request). There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio into pesos; exporters may maintain the foreign currency in non-resident deposit accounts or in foreign-currency accounts with local IFCs, but the proceeds must be registered and channeled through an IFC. For the AI post-production service, the exporter should evidence the service date through completed delivery and invoice documentation, and the sale must be reported to DIAN as an export service under the zero-rated regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Capital) and Operational Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with cross-border FX desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. Under Colombian law, a foreign digital EMI (e.g., Wise or other non-bank electronic money institutions) cannot open a local regulated current or escrow account for a Colombian S.A.S. without holding a license from the Financial Superintendence of Colombia. These entities can provide limited cross-border payment initiation and collection services through approved partnerships with local banks, but they are not permitted to offer deposit-taking or treasury settlement account functionality. As a result, for institutional treasury purposes, a local bank account at an IFC is legally indispensable for executing FX settlements, capital repatriation, and tax payments; an EMI can be used solely as an auxiliary collection rail for micro-subscription receivables, not as the primary liquidity clearing account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no hard statutory requirement that every director appear physically before the bank, but the mandatory KYC due diligence of an S.A.S. corporate client requires the legal representative(s) and, in most cases, the ultimate beneficial owner(s) to complete an in-person or supervised videoconference identity interview with the bank's compliance officer. In practice, Tier-1 Colombian banks will require at least one locally based or physically present legal representative for initial account activation; foreign directors may be verified by notarized powers of attorney and consular authentication. The bank will also require apostilled corporate documents, a valid RUT (Registro Único Tributario), the notarized Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation issued by the Cámara de Comercio, and proof of the company's real economic activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident direct ownership with no physical Colombian commercial establishment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the S.A.S. bylaws, a notarized and apostilled board resolution naming the resident legal representative, the RUT, audited financial statements, a Colombian lease or BPO contract for operational substance, and a detailed corporate organizational chart identifying the ultimate beneficial owner and source of initial capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between written commercial purpose (ISIC 5912 / NAICS 512191) and expected wire traffic from foreign content platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit executed master service agreements with subtitle/dubbing clients, sample AI processing invoices, export service certificates to DIAN, and a list of counterparty bank identifiers, demonstrating that inflows correspond exclusively to fees for intellectual services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus or unusual post-production licensor in sanctioned/disputed territory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a jurisdiction risk matrix, end-user/customer due diligence files, copies of exchange control declarations (Forms to Banco de la República), SWIFT confirmation history, and an AML/CFT compliance manual with risk-based transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Professionally opaque capital injection structure (e.g., foreign shareholder using a holding company)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a chain-of-title document with full backing powers, audited financial statements of the parent, record of FDIC registration of inbound equity capital in Banco de la República (declaration of international investment), and certified wire instructions with purpose code 'Capital injection under Decree 2245/2011'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent FX forward or hedging activity without evidence of a genuine underlying commercial exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a treasury policy, a head-and-hedge matrix collating forecast invoice collections in USD/EUR with Colombian peso operational outflows, and monthly proof of the underlying services contracts creating the currency exposure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign capital contributions into the Colombian S.A.S. can be made by an international SWIFT wire from the investor to the S.A.S.'s local escrow or operational account at an authorized IFC. Before wiring, the investor must file the Form of Foreign Investment Declaration (Inversión Internacional Directa) with Banco de la República via its electronic system, or through the bank, using reporting code P011 under the Foreign Investment Regulations. The inbound wire must clearly state the name of the investor, the Colombian company, and the transaction purpose code 'Capital injection – Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada'. For subscriptions arising from AI post-production service contracts, no special prior license is required, but the declaration must be registered within the first 20 calendar days of the quarter following the operation. The IFC will verify automatic exchange control compliance and issue the corresponding certificate of channeling (certificado de canalización), which will be required for later dividend distribution or sale of shares.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade settlements (licensing fees, subcontractor AI annotation costs, vendor purchases) should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 direct wire instructions denominated in USD/EUR from the local U.S. dollar or euro account at the IFC, with mandatory mention of the purpose code (e.g., 'trade payment for services rendered' or 'royalty payment') and a corresponding certificates of channeling. For larger capital equipment expenditures (e.g., GPU infrastructure), the Colombian S.A.S. may open an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (LC) with a Colombian bank for the benefit of the overseas supplier; however, because the commercial activity is a low-risk service business, the LC should only be used where the supplier requires bank payment undertaking. All outbound payments must be supported by the underlying contract and invoice; for service fees exceeding a valuation threshold, advance transfer pricing documentation must be considered.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (Dividendos/Forwards with local IFCs) for up to 18-month duration
Non-deliverable FX swaps (NDF) referencing the TRM (Representative Market Rate of the Colombian peso) for hedging uncertain USD/COP cash flows
Currency swaps with authorized banks, solely for hedging convertible current-account exposures
FX options (plain vanilla calls/puts) executed over-the-counter in the local market with Maturity Dates aligned to foreign-invoice receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registry renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March each year; renewal covers the 12-month period through 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A fine of up to 17 SMLMV (minimum legal monthly wages) plus daily delay penalties of 1% of the registration fee per month; after 3 months non-renewal, the commercial registry is suspended and the entity may be administratively struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the annual DIAN filing calendar, typically between 10 February and 10 April following each tax year, with the exact due date determined by the first two digits of the company's NIT (tax ID).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 1% of the tax payable per month or fraction thereof, with a minimum of 10 UVT (tax value unit); applicable late-payment interest (roughly 2% per month); possible administrative fines for inaccurate or non-filed returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filed with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ends 31 December; shareholders' approval must occur by 31 March; the approved financial statements must be filed with the Chamber within 30 days thereafter (usually by 30 April).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance triggers fines of up to 12 SMLMV and may prevent the issuance of the annual existence and representation certificate, thereby blocking commercial operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner register update (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales - RBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the same period as the income tax return (generally 10 February through 10 April), pursuant to DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021; also required within one month of any change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Article 641 of the Colombian Tax Code, up to 15,000 UVT (approximately USD 250,000 in 2025), for non-filing, incomplete, or erroneous beneficial ownership information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal industry and commerce tax (Impuesto de Industria y Comercio - ICA) annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal treasury (e.g., Secretaría de Hacienda de la ciudad donde se ejerce la actividad principal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Varies by municipality; commonly due in the April–June period for the immediately preceding fiscal year (e.g., in Bogotá, the general deadline is on 30 April).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest (approx. 2% per month), fines ranging from 10% to 25% of the unpaid tax, and potential suspension of the business activity permit for repeated non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (revisor fiscal) applies when total assets exceed 30,000 UVT (approx. USD 1.4 million) or gross annual income exceeds 30,000 UVT; also required for companies subject to the supervision of the Superintendencia de Sociedades, when the SAS is considered a public-interest entity, or where cross-border investment exceeds applicable regulatory thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Colombia (NIIF), fully aligned with IASB standards; small and medium entities use NIIF para PYMES; microenterprises use the simplified technical framework if they meet the size parameters under Decree 2420 of 2015.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Register all ultimate beneficial owners (individuals holding directly or indirectly 10% or more of the capital, voting rights, or effective control) in the DIAN RBF within the annual tax filing window (usually February–April); any post-filing change in shareholding or control must be reported within one month. A copy of the RBF confirmation must be kept in the corporate book for audit purposes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registro de Representantes Legales)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas y Juntas Directivas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 700 per year for a registered office or commercial agent service in Bogotá or Medellín
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – USD 8,000 per year for a standard independent audit (where applicable) for a small to medium Colombian SAS

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying creative-economy and digital-content producers may benefit from the preferential 7% corporate income tax tariff established by Law 1955 of 2019 (Article 176) for activities registered as orange economy ventures, subject to meeting specific Ministry of Culture registration and annual compliance requirements. Additionally, eligible investment in research, science, technology, and innovation software at the entity level can generate a 100% additional tax deduction on such expenditure, effectively reducing the effective tax rate for profitable, innovation-intensive subtitle AI and voice cloning businesses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) filed electronically through the DIAN Muisca system (https://www.muisca.dian.gov.co)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline is assigned by DIAN based on the last two digits of the SAS’s NIT; for a fiscal year ending 31 December, the filing deadline falls in the April–May window of the following year (generally between April 9 and May 21).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National Tax Identification Number of the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NIT is automatically assigned to the Colombian SAS; the beneficial non-resident parent or shareholder has no separate NIT entry and does not file this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All revenue earned from audio post-production, subtitle transcription, AI voice-cloning licensing, and technology services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include global revenue of the Colombian entity; non-resident shareholders should not allocate their own revenue to this line. The Colombian entity is the sole domestic taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 50 — Deductions and Cost of Sale
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs such as staff, cloud AI infrastructure, remuneration to foreign subcontractors, depreciation of sound-editing equipment, and direct production costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any payment to non-resident suppliers must be entered in the corresponding cross-border payment annex and must be supported by withholding tax certificates for payments subject to source tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after applying 35% ordinary corporate tariff or the preferential 7% orange-economy tariff, plus any deductible R&D incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident entry; this is the final taxable base after statutory deductions, exemptions, and loss carryforwards (maximum 5 years).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 78 — Income Tax after Tariff Application
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result of applying 35% ordinary rate or 7% preferential creative-economy rate to taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The entity computes the tax; non-resident shareholders only face dividend WHT upon distribution as reported in Annex 16 (dividends paid abroad).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after deducting withholding tax credits, prepayments, and industry-specific discounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any withholding tax already retained by the entity on cross-border payments is shown by the SAP, not by the non-resident beneficiary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing carries a monetary fine of 5% per month of the total assessed tax payable, capped at 100% of the assessed tax; when no tax is due, fixed late-filing fines apply (approximately COP 500,000 per month of delay). Delayed payment additionally accrues monthly default interest at the legal rate. Sanctions for omission of annex information or transfer pricing forms start at 1% of related-party transactions and can reach 32,000 UVT.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% headline rate; a 35% withholding rate applies where the dividend distribution is sourced from profits not already taxed at the entity level (e.g., preferential 7% orange-economy profits).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, together with the Form 380 or equivalent DIAN declaration, and a beneficial ownership statement. The Colombian payer files the reduced-rate withholding through the Muisca system before the payment deadline; the DIAN may request the TRC within the subsequent five-year audit window.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties on IP software and AI dubbing licenses: statutory 15% withholding, generally reduced to 10% under Colombia DTAs (e.g., Spain, UK, US). Interest on external debt: statutory 10% for registered foreign loans meeting extended-term requirements (15% for unregistered or short-term balances), with treaty rates typically capped at 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: COP 250 million transactional figure in an annual period triggers inclusion in the Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Form 2280) and related-party annex; full Local File and Master File documentation is compulsory when the taxpayer’s gross income or gross assets equal or exceed approximately COP 11.8 billion for the tax year 2024 (threshold measured in 250,000 UVT).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not operate the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the tax authorities apply substance-over-form principles, the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR), and the abusive tax planning regime. A SAS that merely routes licensing royalty streams through apparently related parties without personnel, premises, or decision-making substance may be recharacterized as a shell company and subject to substantial penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Declaration in Corporate Income Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating streamed subtitle or voice-clone licensing revenue, inflating deductions for sham subcontracts, or suppressing registration of foreign royalty payments due to artificial transfer pricing and channeling transactions to lower-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under Article 335 of the Colombian Criminal Code carries imprisonment of 36 to 60 months and a fine up to 1,500 SMMLV (statutory monthly minimum wages) in addition to collection of unpaid tax, default interest, and a 200% surcharge on the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false returns or participate in evasion may be criminally prosecuted, barred from holding board positions, subjected to embargo of personal assets, and prevented from leaving Colombia (judicial exit ban).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abusive Structure Under Corporate Veil Rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the SAS with no real operational activity in Colombia, no local personnel, no technical equipment, and using the entity solely as an empty conduit for AI royalties while the actual post-production work is performed abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 1258 of 2008 (SAS Law), the court or DIAN may pierce the corporate veil and disallow the entity’s separate tax identity, imposing corporate income tax at the underlying foreign beneficiary level plus penalties. GAAR penalties can be up to 200% of the tax avoided and suspension of any preferential tariff.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts when personal assets are used to manipulate the entity’s capital or when the corporate form is used to commit fraud; risk includes civil restitution, travel bans, and confiscation of personal property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering Through Artificial Transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the subtitle and dubbing studio’s Stripe or Wise payment rails to layer funds from alleged AI services with fake contracts, blowing up invoices to move foreign currency without truth of operation, or transacting with politically exposed persons without AML checks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under Article 323 of the Colombian Criminal Code is punishable by 10 to 20 years’ imprisonment and a fine of up to 20,000 SMMLV for serious commercial arrangements. The proceeds and related assets are subject to forfeiture, even if the underlying tax claim is minor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be individually indicted for money laundering, internet-order travel bans are replaced by preventive detention, and authorities can confiscate passports; directors may also face derivative liability for civil restitution equal to the laundered amount to investors.
